proxy_language: Proto-Kartvelian (reconstructed, ca. 4th-3rd millennium BCE) as a speculative proxy for the Trialetian Mesolithic/Epipaleolithic hunter-gatherer culture of the South Caucasus
proxy_rationale: The Trialetian (ca. 12,000-8,000 BCE, Trialeti/Kotias Klde/Satsurblia region) is known only archaeologically; its language is unknown and Pleistocene-Holocene hunter-gatherers there left no linguistic trace. The only defensible choice is a reconstructed language family of the same geographic region: Proto-Kartvelian (Georgian, Svan, Zan/Mingrelian-Laz), with its famous consonant clusters and ablaut-based roots. This is separated from the culture by 5,000+ years and may not be descended from it at all (the region also hosted North Caucasian and later Indo-European, Hurro-Urartian and Semitic speakers), so the link is purely areal and should be treated as flavour, not as a claim.
phonology: Proto-Kartvelian (Klimov, Fahnrich, Gamkrelidze-Mach'avariani) is reconstructed with a three-way laryngeal-like contrast in stops and affricates (voiced, aspirated/voiceless, ejective/glottalized): *b *p *p' / *d *t *t' / *g *k *k' / *q *q' (uvular), affricates *dz *ts *ts' and *dz-hat *c-hat *c-hat' (palatal series, written j/c/c' in some conventions), sibilants *s *z *s-hat *z-hat, fricatives *x *gh (velar/uvular), liquids *r *l, nasals *m *n, glides *w *y. Vowels: *a *e *i *o *u (with *a/*e alternating in ablaut). Here the romanization used for the game is a simplified Georgian-style scheme: ejectives written plain/with apostrophe, palatal sibilants written sh zh ch.
phonotactics: Syllable template (C)(C)(C)V(C)(C); Kartvelian is known for heavy initial and medial clusters (e.g. Georgian prtskvni, mtsvrtneli) with harmonic clusters (e.g. gv-, br-, tsq-). Roots are mostly CVC or CCVC with ablaut (a/e ~ zero grade). Words may end in a vowel or a consonant; Georgian nominatives end in -i, Svan/Zan have their own endings. No phonemic stress in the proto-language; Georgian has weak initial-syllable stress. For game purposes keep clusters of 2-3 consonants at word onset, 1-2 at coda.
orthography: Use a scholarly Latin transliteration of Georgian-type phonology: plain letters b d g k p t q z s x r l m n v j y; digraphs sh zh ch ts dz kh gh; ejectives optionally marked with an apostrophe after the letter (k' p' t' q' ts' ch'). Reconstructed forms are marked with an asterisk in the notes/roots list but not in the names themselves. Vowels a e i o u only; no long vowels or diacritics required.
morphology: Agglutinating/polypersonal; roots are mostly verbal or nominal with ablaut. Georgian-type noun morphology: nominative -i, ergative -ma, genitive -is(a), dative -s(a), instrumental -it, adverbial -ad; plural -eb. Derivational prefixes/suffixes: mo-...-e (agent, 'one who'), sa-...-o (place/instrument, 'a place for X'), m-...-e (agentive), -oba/-ba (abstract nouns), -uri/-ur (adjectival 'belonging to'), -eli (agent/participle), -ar/-ian (possessive), tsa- and ga- (directional preverbs). Diminutive -a/-uka. For naming, derive from roots with sa-...-e/o for places and tools and -i/-a as citation endings.
compounding: Compounds are head-final in nouns: modifier + head (e.g. Georgian mta-wvera 'mountain-peak'). Genitive constructions place the possessor before the possessed in -is/-s (e.g. mtis-tskali 'mountain-water'); dependency 'X of Y' is rendered as Y-is X or Y-X compound. Adjectives precede nouns in Georgian (lamazi kali 'beautiful woman'). Agent compounds: object + verbal root + -eli ('X-maker'), e.g. ghvin-is-mts'q'ob-eli. Place names are often formed with sa-ROOT-e/o or ROOT-eti (Trialeti: -eti is a collective/locative suffix, 'place of ...').
noun_phrase_order: Modifier-head: adjective + noun, possessor (genitive) + possessed, numeral + noun; demonstrative + adjective + noun. Postpositions rather than prepositions (-ze 'on', -shi 'in', -tan 'near', -gan 'from').

attested_roots.gloss: mother (reduplicated child-word; cf. Georgian deda, Svan dada)
god (Georgian ghmerti, Mingrelian ghoronti, Svan ghermet)

notes: Speculative areal proxy only: no linguistic evidence ties Trialetian hunter-gatherers to Kartvelian, which may be a later arrival or a later spread. Current game strings (Radzi isy dexa, Gilag isy betentsa, Tsuli, Moshade, Laqon, Radzeyon) are not Kartvelian-structured (e.g. 'isy', 'ts' + y vowel patterns); names should be rebuilt with Kartvelian-style clusters (tsq-, mts-, br-, sh-, kh-), nominative -i/-a/-e, sa-...-e place frames, genitive -is and modifier-head order. Not Diaithiris. No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word, since the language is not Goidelic.
